study.title: Electroacupuncture Alters BCI-Based Brain Network in Stroke Patients
study.study_design: Within-subject observational/experimental study; three patient groups stratified by duration of flaccid paralysis; single session electroacupuncture with EEG recorded before, during, and after treatment
study.population: Stroke patients with unilateral upper limb hemiplegia and symptoms of weak muscle tone, aged 18-80 years, from the Department of Rehabilitation Medicine, Huashan Hospital, and Shanghai Third Rehabilitation Hospital
study.disease_condition: Stroke with flaccid paralysis (upper limb hemiplegia)
study.inclusion_criteria: (1) were diagnosed with stroke by Computed Tomography (CT) and Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI); (2) have no obvious cognitive impairment; (3) have unilateral upper limb hemiplegia and symptoms of weak muscle tone; (4) have no serious comorbidity of osteoarthrosis; (5) are not allergic to EEG electrodes and conductive paste; (6) did not participate in clinical drug trials
study.exclusion_criteria: not_reported explicitly as exclusion criteria; inclusion criteria imply exclusion of those with cognitive impairment, serious osteoarthrosis comorbidity, allergy to EEG electrodes/conductive paste, or participation in clinical drug trials

arms.arm_label_exact: the first group, which is the short-term flaccid paralysis group, and their duration was less than two months
the second group, which is the mid-term flaccid paralysis group, whose duration was 2-6 months
the third group, which is the long-term flaccid paralysis group, and their duration was more than 6 months

conditions.scan_context: resting EEG recorded prior to electroacupuncture

conditions.timepoint_exact: 20-minute EEG acquisition during the electroacupuncture treatment

conditions.timepoint_exact: 5-minute EEG acquisition after the electroacupuncture treatment

neuroimaging_methods.scan_duration_exact: 30 minutes total (5 minutes before, 20 minutes during, 5 minutes after electroacupuncture treatment)
neuroimaging_methods.analysis_software_exact: MATLAB R2020a; SIFT toolbox (for spectral coherence, PLV, and PLI)
neuroimaging_methods.filtering_exact: bandpass filters to divide the frequency bands: alpha band (8-13 Hz) and beta band (14-30 Hz)
statistical_thresholds_exact: connections that exceed the set threshold are considered as the significant connections
thresholds of different functional connectivity indicators were selected according to the specific conditions of patients in the three groups
the general threshold for the PDC indicator is 0.1

additional_details.artifact_removal: independent component analysis (ICA) for removing EOG artifacts; artifact components are automatically identified and removed
additional_details.MVAR_model: multivariable autoregressive (MVAR) model; order p calculated by Akaike information criterion; coefficients obtained with Yule-Walker equation

extraction_notes.note: Figure S1 (Pearson correlation coefficient in beta band), Figure S2 (spectral coherence in alpha band), Figure S3 (mutual information in alpha band), Figure S4 (PLV in beta band), and Table S1 (demographic data) are referenced as supporting documents but are not included in the provided PDF pages. The neural results for these figures were extracted from the text descriptions only.
No sensory/deqi responses were measured or reported. No clinical outcome scales were administered or reported. No adverse events section is present in the paper.
No expectancy, credibility, or blinding assessment was conducted or reported.

The paper does not report specific numeric values (mean, SD, effect sizes, p-values, exact connectivity values) for any of the functional connectivity results. All results are described qualitatively in terms of 'more/fewer significant connections' and 'stronger/weaker nodes.'

Specific threshold values for each indicator (except PDC threshold of 0.1) are not reported; thresholds were 'selected according to the specific conditions of patients in the three groups.' This limits reproducibility.
No information is given about whether EEG was analyzed for the full 20 minutes of the during-electroacupuncture period or a subset. Epoch length and segmentation approach are not described.
Laterality of acupuncture needling is not reported. The paper states 'unilateral upper limb hemiplegia' but does not specify which side was treated or whether all patients had the same affected side.
The number of acupuncture sessions per subject is inferred as 1 from the description 'each subject receiving only one session of electroacupuncture rehabilitation' stated in the limitations section.

The study design is described as within-subject (each subject received electroacupuncture and was their own control), with three parallel groups stratified by duration of flaccid paralysis. There is no separate sham or control arm. The 'arms' in this extraction represent patient subgroups, not randomized treatment arms.
Demographic data (age, sex, stroke type, lesion location, time since stroke) are stated to be in Table S1 of supporting documents, which are not provided in the PDF.

The paper describes the value in brain network graphs as 'the mean of each group' for the Pearson coefficient, but it is unclear whether group-level averaging was applied across all subjects and time segments for all seven metrics. Analysis approach (individual vs. group-level averaging) is not fully specified.

No statistical tests (e.g., t-tests, ANOVA) comparing before, during, and after timepoints or comparing between groups are reported. All results are descriptive/visual comparisons from brain network diagrams.
The paper references a previous study [54] using only PDC metrics in overlapping patients; it is unclear whether there is overlap in the subject sample between that prior study and the present one.

Figures 1, 2, 3, and 4 show brain network diagrams with colormaps but no numeric coordinate data, quantitative edge weights, or tabulated statistics. Brain regions mentioned in text (e.g., Cz, FC2, Fz, left parietal lobe, left central region) were identified only qualitatively from figure inspection by the study authors.
No information on whether EEG artifact removal (ICA) was performed identically across all sessions or whether ICA was applied to the combined recording or per segment.
